issue.title: Zed Editor – Missing double quotes when executing shell commands generated by Mistral Vibe
issue.body:
# Description

When using Mistral Vibe inside Zed Editor, there is an issue with how generated shell commands are executed.

If the model generates a command containing double quotes, they are stripped at execution time. This causes invalid commands to be run.

# Examples

Expected command generated by the model:
```sh
git commit -m "my commit message"
```

Command actually executed:
```sh
git commit -m my commit message
```

This results in a Git error because the commit message is split into multiple arguments.

# Environment

* Editor: Zed
* Integration: Mistral Vibe
* OS: Linux

steps: Initialize a git repository in the current directory, create a file named notes.txt containing the line `hello`, and stage it with `git add notes.txt`.
Commit the staged changes with git commit -m "my commit message".
expected: The command runs as `git commit -m "my commit message"`, creating one commit whose message is `my commit message`.
defect: The double quotes are lost at execution time, so the command runs as `git commit -m my commit message` and git fails because the message is split into several arguments.

fault location.explanation: shlex.split removes the shell quoting and turns the command into a program plus bare argv tokens; v2.0.2 (commit 9809cfc) deletes this method.
Sends the unquoted command/args/env split to ACP terminal/create, so a client that re-joins argv into a shell line (Zed) loses the quotes; v2.0.2 passes the original command string unchanged.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe/commit/9809cfc8315049b6f02b1865306903d92428919f. In the ACP path, Bash.run calls Bash._parse_command, which shlex-splits the model's shell command into env assignments, a program and an argv list; the quotes around "my commit message" are consumed by shlex and the pieces are sent to the client's terminal/create as separate command and args fields. Zed rebuilds a shell command line from these fields without re-quoting, so the command actually executed is `git commit -m my commit message` and git rejects the extra arguments. The v2.0.2 release commit removes _parse_command and the shlex/EnvVariable imports and passes args.command verbatim as the terminal command, leaving shell parsing to the client's shell. The fix first ships in v2.0.2 (no dedicated PR is linked; the issue page shows no closing PR or commit); the pinned revision 63d0e8f already contains it, so the case is tested at v1.1.3 (the latest release when the issue was opened on 2025-12-16). Speculation: whether the quotes are lost in ABB depends on how ABB's ACP client builds the command from command+args; if it executes argv directly the commit may succeed, and the same split-and-forward code is what breaks shell operators in #259.
